blockers.description: CMS crashes: `The requested module 'fs-extra' does not provide an export named 'existsSync'`. Node.js 20.20.0 loadESMFromCJS loads .js files with ESM import syntax via ESM runtime; named imports from CJS packages with dynamic module.exports (like fs-extra) fail. After fs-extra there may be more packages with same issue.
blockers.workaround: Extend fix-lodash-fp.js to also patch fs-extra. After the existing lodash forEach, add: const fse = require('/app/node_modules/fs-extra'); const fseKeys = Object.keys(fse); build fp.mjs-style wrapper at /app/node_modules/fs-extra/index.mjs; patch /app/node_modules/fs-extra/package.json exports map with '.' + './index' + './index.js' all pointing to index.mjs for import and index.js for require. Check for nested fs-extra under @strapi/* too. Rebuild. Then check for next error.

decisions.decision: loadESMFromCJS in Node.js 20.20.0 is root cause: dist/src/index.js (compiled TS with ESM syntax) is require()d by Strapi CJS core, loaded as ESM, which chain-loads other ESM imports that fail on named CJS imports
decisions.rationale: Understanding the root cause: our TS compiles to ESM .js files, Strapi loads them via require(), Node 20.20.0 uses loadESMFromCJS to handle them as ESM. Named imports from CJS modules with non-static exports fail in ESM context.

context_notes: This session (2026-03-23) did 6 CMS rebuilds. Root cause of all failures: Node.js 20.20.0 loadESMFromCJS feature. When Strapi CJS core loads our compiled dist/src/index.js via require(), it sees ESM syntax and uses loadESMFromCJS. This loads it as ESM. In ESM context, named imports from CJS packages (lodash/fp, fs-extra) fail unless the package has statically-detectable named exports. Fix: create .mjs wrapper with explicit named exports + package.json exports map. Applied to lodash (all 19 nested installs patched). fs-extra is next. Pattern is clear and mechanical. Commits pushed this session: 3025c89, 1c148dc, 10c34d6, 5f53f96, 5227e62.
